Debit Note — Edit

The Debit Note form enables you to record claims against suppliers for returns, allowances, or corrections to previously received purchase invoices.

Debit notes are formal documents that reduce the amount you owe to suppliers. They serve as the opposite of credit notes - while credit notes reduce what customers owe you, debit notes reduce what you owe suppliers.

When to Use Debit Notes

Issue debit notes when returning goods to suppliers, claiming damages, receiving pricing adjustments, or correcting errors in supplier invoices. The debit note creates a negative balance in the supplier's account that can be offset against future purchases or refunded.

Creating a Debit Note

When creating a debit note, specify the supplier and clearly state the reason for the debit. Include details of returned items with quantities and values, or describe the nature of any pricing disputes or quality issues.

Reference the original purchase invoice when applicable. The system will automatically adjust inventory levels if physical goods are being returned to the supplier. Multiple line items can be included with appropriate expense accounts and tax codes.

Form Fields

This form contains the following fields:

Issue date

Enter the date when this debit note is issued to the supplier.

This date determines when the debit reduces what you owe the supplier and appears in your accounts payable.

Reference

Enter a reference number for this debit note. This helps track and identify the debit note in supplier communications.

You can use automatic numbering or enter your own reference, such as the supplier's credit memo number.

Supplier

Select the supplier to whom this debit note is issued. This determines the currency and affects your payables.

The debit note will reduce what you owe this supplier and can be applied against their outstanding invoices.

Purchase Invoice

Optionally, link this debit note to a specific purchase invoice. This helps track which invoice is being adjusted and can automatically apply the debit.

If linked to an invoice, the debit will automatically reduce that specific invoice's balance.

Exchange rate

If the supplier uses a foreign currency, enter the exchange rate for converting to your base currency.

The exchange rate should match the rate used when recording the original purchase to avoid exchange differences.

Description

Optionally, add a description or reason for this debit note, such as 'Goods returned' or 'Price adjustment agreed'.

This description helps document why the debit was issued and appears in reports for audit trail purposes.

Lines

Enter the line items being debited. Each line represents a product or service with the amount to be deducted from what you owe.

Line items should match what was originally purchased, using the same accounts and tax codes for accuracy.

Amounts are tax inclusive

Check this box if the amounts you enter already include tax. Leave unchecked if tax should be calculated separately.

This setting should match how the original purchase invoice was recorded to ensure correct tax calculations.

Column — Line number

Check this box to display line numbers on the debit note. This helps reference specific items with suppliers.

Line numbers are useful when discussing specific items with suppliers or matching to their credit memo.

Column — Description

Check this box to show a description column for each line item, allowing detailed explanations for each debit.

Descriptions help explain why each item is being debited, especially for quality issues or agreed adjustments.

Column — Discount

Check this box to enable a discount column if the debit relates to discount adjustments.

Use this when the debit note is for retrospective discounts or pricing adjustments agreed with the supplier.

Also acts as goods receipt

Check this box if this debit note also represents a return of physical goods to the supplier, updating inventory levels.

When checked, the debit note will also reduce your inventory quantities for the returned items.

PurchaseInventoryLocation

Select the inventory location from which goods are being returned to the supplier.

This determines which warehouse or location's inventory will be reduced for the returned items.
